summary: The required result needs only a constant number of array property reads, and the accepted implementation achieves the smallest possible asymptotic time class, leaving no genuine slower principal class for scaling.

optimality.argument: Producing any result requires at least one constant-time decision, establishing an Omega(1) lower bound independent of array length n. The accepted method reads length once and performs at most one indexed access, so its upper bound is O(1).

replacement_checks.evidence: Every implementation must make at least one constant-time decision to distinguish an empty receiver from a returned value.
The accepted source performs one length comparison and, only for a non-empty array, one direct indexed property access.
Cases cover empty and single-element arrays plus null, false, negative one, strings, objects, nested arrays, and mixed JSON values without mutation.
